body:
Maintainer ruling (2026-08-25, in-session batch adjudication; verbatim: 「就全部接受，然后继续下一批」): **Option B** — production bundles emit a rate-limited, deduplicated warning (one per distinct failing predicate) when a `visibleWhen` / node-gate predicate faults, replacing the current `__DEV__`-only silence. Options C (telemetry, couples to unfinished #5522) and D (host switch, new public config surface) are rejected for now; A is rejected — the silence is no longer an accepted property.

Implementation constraints from the ruling discussion: dedup keyed per predicate source (not per render); negligible-bundle-cost requirement stands; keep this **observability-only** — the fail-open semantics themselves are NOT changed by this card, and the wiring fix for the `/forms/:name` scope gap (#6262) lands in its own PR, not this one.

State transition: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (label swap by triage; if the label lags, this comment is the authoritative record). Lane `domain:ui`; type Task; S–M.

## `pm:retriage` — this card is labelled dispatchable and reads as a decision

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`.
⛔ No label removed, no grading changed — `pm:retriage` attached alongside, dissent in the same
stroke.

### The mismatch

The card carries `pm:queue` and **no `type`**, but everything in it says it is not work:

- the title is `[Decision]`;
- the body states outright: *"⛔ The PM seat does not rule it, and ⚠️ triage may re-grade the label
  — it is applied here to make the card visible in the inbox, not as a triage product"*;
- the question it asks — what diagnostic budget production should carry for a faulting
  `visibleWhen` — is a design call with a stated cost table, not a defect with a landing site;
- #5926 (`type: Bug`) records `Blocked-by: #6038`.

`pm:queue` is the label that says *"a dev can be pointed at this today"*. On this card it is
saying that about a question nobody has answered, and the escalating seat wrote as much into the
body. ⚠️ The inbox is `needs-user-decision`; `pm:queue` is not a visibility mechanism.

### Why it matters more than the usual mislabel

It gates a Bug. #5926 cannot come back to the queue until this is ruled, so as long as this card
sits in the *dispatchable* pool rather than the *decision* pool, the block on #5926 is invisible
to the only sweep that would move it — and the most likely outcome is a dev being spent on a
design question, returning `needs_decision` with zero code, which is exactly what the bounce
clause exists to catch late rather than early.

### What I am asking for

A first touch: a `type`, and either `needs-user-decision` (my reading — it is a design question
with a maintainer-facing cost table, and the four-facet block is already in the body) or an
explicit ruling that it is chartered work, in which case I will dispatch it as graded.

⛔ Not dispatching it in the meantime — `pm:retriage` keeps it out of selection while the
dissent is open, which is the protection I want here.

## ⚠️ My dissent was wrong — withdrawn. Claimed + dispatched.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`,
branch `claude/issue-6038-visiblewhen-fault-warning`.

**The maintainer ruled this card at 2026-08-25T05:50Z — about sixteen hours before I claimed it
was unruled.** I read the `[Decision]` title, the body's *"the PM seat does not rule it"*, and the
missing `type`, concluded the card was a decision sitting in the dispatchable queue, and filed a
dissent. The ruling was in the comment thread the whole time, and that comment even anticipates
this: *"if the label lags, this comment is the authoritative record."* The body line I leaned on
was written **before** the ruling and had simply gone stale.

⭐ My own pre-dispatch gate's step (a) is **read the whole comment thread — not the body, not the
labels**. I ran a careful check against the title, the body and the labels, and never read the
thread that had the answer. That is the same failure shape I have been cataloguing all round: the
check was run, against the wrong surface. Recording it here because a dissent that cost the triage
seat a re-judgement should not be quietly deleted.

What the dissent did surface was real but much smaller: the label lag and the unset `type`, both
now repaired by triage in one stroke.

### The charter — the ruling comment, quoted verbatim as triage instructed

Maintainer, 2026-08-25, in-session batch adjudication (verbatim): 「就全部接受，然后继续下一批」
⇒ **Option B**.

> production bundles emit a rate-limited, deduplicated warning (one per distinct failing
> predicate) when a `visibleWhen` / node-gate predicate faults, replacing the current `__DEV__`-only
> silence. Options C (telemetry, couples to unfinished #5522) and D (host switch, new public config
> surface) are rejected for now; A is rejected — the silence is no longer an accepted property.

> Implementation constraints from the ruling discussion: dedup keyed **per predicate source (not
> per render)**; negligible-bundle-cost requirement stands; keep this **observability-only** — the
> fail-open semantics themselves are **NOT** changed by this card, and the wiring fix for the
> `/forms/:name` scope gap (#6262) lands in its own PR, not this one.

### Pre-dispatch gate

- **(a) Whole thread read** — 4 records, this time actually read: the escalation, the maintainer
  ruling, my (withdrawn) dissent, triage's re-judgement.
- **(b) Shadow check, in-flight and batch.** In flight: #6373 (`plugin-dashboard` +
  `types/data-display.ts`), #6034 (`app-shell` confirm runtimes), #6397 (`packages/types`
  `PartialSchema` pin, same batch). ⛔ **#6262 is a `needs-user-decision` card in this lane and its
  `/forms/:name` wiring is explicitly excluded by the ruling** — do not touch it.
- **(c) Call-site census** — the dev's, on its own branch: enumerate every predicate-fault catch
  site the warning must cover, and prove the dedup key is the predicate *source*, not the render.

⚠️ **The bounce-clause concern in my dissent is moot** — the decision is made and on the record.
A `needs_decision` return on this card would now be wrong.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, with **Clause-② recorded** (the report did not flag it)

PR #6446, head `3893507fc`. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session
`session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Verified on a pinned ref (`refs/pmtmp/6038`).

### ⚠️ Clause-② applies — a widened public surface, stated here because nobody stated it

Two additions the report's summary does not name as surface changes:

1. **`packages/react/src/index.ts` exports four new symbols** —
   `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate`, `formatUnresolvableVisibilityMessage`,
   `UNRESOLVABLE_VISIBILITY_PREFIX`, `__resetVisibilityPredicateWarnings`.
2. **`packages/core` adds `EvaluationOptions.onFault?: (reason: string) => void`** to a published
   options type.

⭐ The widening is **justified, and the reason is load-bearing rather than convenience** — it is
written beside the export: `page:tabs` item predicates live in `@object-ui/components`, which
depends on `@object-ui/react`; a second copy of the reporter would mean **a second rate limit**,
so the same broken predicate would be entitled to one line *per package* instead of one line.
The export is what makes the ruling's "one per distinct source" true *across* packages.

⛔ This does **not** block: the standing order is that Clause-② goes **at-tier, straight to the
queue** (「直接入队」). But it belongs on the record, and ⚠️ one member is worth a reviewer's eye:
**`__resetVisibilityPredicateWarnings` is a test hook on the package entry.** Common for resettable
module state, but it publishes something only tests need.

The changeset declares `patch` across all three packages. `Changeset Bump Policy`,
`Changeset Declaration` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are all green on this head, so that is
the repo's mechanically-enforced convention for an additive change, not a judgement I need to
second-guess.

### ⭐ The premise was measured, and it is narrower than the card claimed

The card says production prints nothing. That is true of **one dialect of three**:

| predicate form | production before |
|---|---|
| bare string | **silent** |
| `{ dialect: 'cel' }` envelope | one generic deduped line |
| `${…}` template | one generic line **per evaluation** — the flood the ruling's rate-limit clause exists for |

⭐ The silent dialect is the bare string, which is precisely the one objectstack#11254 measured a
live gate breaking on — **so the card stands, for a narrower and better-evidenced reason than it
gave.** All three now converge on one node-bearing line per distinct source. Correcting a card's
premise while confirming its conclusion is the right result, not a complication.

### The blocker it had to solve, and why the seam is the right shape

`throwOnError` — the only existing fault-detection channel — makes `evaluateCelCondition`
**evaluate twice**. Using it would have paid for observability with double the engine calls on the
production path. `EvaluationOptions.onFault` is a passback reporting the fault the evaluator has
**already caught inside its existing catch**, so production pays the same number of calls —
⭐ pinned with a counting getter (passback == plain call; the `throwOnError` probe strictly more),
which turns "no extra cost" into a measurement rather than a claim.

### The moved pin is the legitimate case, and it is documented in the code

An existing pin — `SchemaRenderer.visibleWhenRecordBinding`, *"a PRODUCTION build … prints
nothing"* — asserted **the exact property the ruling retires**. It was rewritten:

```
- expect(…).toHaveLength(0);
+ // This assertion used to read `toHaveLength(0)`, and the change is the …
+ expect(produced).toHaveLength(2);
```

Old value, new value and the clause that moves it, all **beside the assertion** where the next
reader finds them — not only in the PR body. Verdicts unchanged. That is exactly the standard for
moving a pin.

### The observability-only constraint, as a measurement

⭐ **Every verdict assertion stayed GREEN in both ablation legs.** Leg A predicted 9 failed / 5
passed and measured exactly that, with the failing case names matching the predicted set; leg B
predicted 4/3 and measured 4/3. **The change moves the silence, not the answer** — which is the
ruling's constraint demonstrated rather than asserted. Mutation proven on disk by blob hash *and*
marker counts before any reading; restore verified by hash plus empty `git diff HEAD`.

### Bundle cost measured A/B, not argued

A detached compare worktree pinned to this branch's **base** `9602dc820` (deliberately not
`origin/main`, which a sibling agent's fetch had already advanced) — **+107 bytes gzipped** total
across the two chunks carrying the change; every per-chunk ceiling unmoved. And the structural
reason: the reporter module **already shipped** in every production bundle, because `__DEV__` is a
runtime IIFE over `globalThis.process?.env?.NODE_ENV`, not the member expression bundlers
constant-fold — so it was never tree-shaken and only the wiring is new. That satisfies the
ruling's negligible-bundle-cost requirement with evidence.

### Scope and file surface

The file surface is **wider than my dispatch anticipated** — `packages/core/src/evaluator/` and
`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx` beyond `packages/react` — and it is named
with evidence in the PR body rather than arriving silently. Shadow-checked: #6108 also holds
`packages/core`, but at `src/utils/column-sortability.ts` — **different file, no overlap**.

⛔ #6262 untouched, as the ruling required. #5687's adapter-only leg kept dev-only under its own
ruling and **pinned silent in production** — a negative pin, which is the right way to record a
deliberate exclusion. Census: 7 predicate-fault catch sites by shape — 2 fixed, 3 filed
(#6443 / #6444 / #6445), 2 already loud and untouched.

### Landing

⛔ Not enqueued — 18 green, **10 still running**, 0 failures, `behind` (⛔ not syncing).
